requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs` has no incoming `{impl}` references or `:impl:` anchors, and the review roots are empty. I checked whether it states any structural property that would need implementation evidence, and it states none.

Every clause describes what the harness observably does when it builds the mandatory input set:
- "every direct implementation reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source selection to the initial mandatory inputs". The harness could build this set in a loop, a pipeline or a table lookup and still give the same inputs.
- "An in-source reference selects its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline; an anchor selects its named file or node". This defines which selection is produced. No type, field or signature is prescribed.
- "Source access, exclusions, errors, and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules". This defers to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, which is a behavioral requirement.
- "Refining declarations continue to contribute their complete text" is an input-content rule.
- "Implementation helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively" fixes when inputs are supplied. It does not fix how the code is organized.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, ownership rule or delegation through a named interface. An alternative implementation could produce identical mandatory inputs with different internal structure and still satisfy every clause. So no structural obligation needs implementation evidence, and I found no gap.

behavioral: The tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`. I did not read the implementation. I judged the tests against the requirement text and the three supplied test items.

- **Whole file when there is no outline.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[plain_implementation_reference_supplies_the_entire_file_as_the_only_root]` writes a `notes.txt` file with a plain `{impl}` reference. It asserts exactly one file input with `item` equal to `""` and the full text, so the reference selects the whole file.
- **Enclosing outline node.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]` uses an in-source `{impl}` reference above `pub fn api`. It asserts that the root is `fn[api]`, that its text contains `helper();`, and that it does not contain `fn helper`. The last two assertions show that the review does not recurse into helpers. Later in the same test the `:impl:` anchor is removed and only the source reference remains. The test still finds an `fn[api]` input, so the reference alone selects its enclosing node.
- **Anchors.** The same test uses an `:impl:` anchor naming `fn[api]`. It also checks that an implementation anchor alone, with no in-source reference, still gives a review root. `structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules` uses a whole-file anchor on `evidence/generated.rs` and asserts that file appears as an input.
- **Deduplication.** The anchor and the in-source reference select the same node, and the test asserts that there is exactly one `src/lib.rs` root.
- **Existing rules for access, exclusions and errors.** `structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules` covers a gitignored file, which fails with an error containing "excluded". It covers an anchor naming a missing node, which fails with an error containing "missing". It covers the allowed `evidence/` file.
- **Incoming test references and anchors do not stop impl roots.** The test adds a `{test}` reference and checks that `fn[api]` is still an input. It also converts the `:impl:` anchor to `:test:` and checks that `review_roots` is still present. `removing_either_root_changes_the_evidence_but_keeps_both_checks` covers all four impl/test combinations. For each one, the structural prompt includes `api.md` only when an implementation edge exists.
- **Out-of-scope subjects.** An example, and a distributed requirement with a `sites` block, give no review roots and no `src/lib.rs` input.
- **Refining declarations.** A refining requirement with an `{impl}` marker in its text contributes its complete text, as `[":::{req} refined", impl_role, "Refinement.", ":::"]`. It contributes no file input, even though the unreferenced `src/lib.rs` exists.

I found no obligation that lacks a test with a relevant assertion.

text: :::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
